brief.title: The Gaslamp Quay
brief.premise: A tide-clock inspector in a fog-bound port city investigates the death of a lamplighter found drowned in a locked lamp-house, and discovers that the harbour board has been selling false curfews.
constraints: Nothing supernatural: every event must have a natural explanation.

world.name: Gaslamp Quay
world.description: Gaslamp Quay is a fog-bound estuary port lit by coal gas and ruled by the Harbour Board, where curfews are bought and sold.

locations.name: Lamp-House Row
locations.description: A terrace of locked lamp-houses where gas lamps are filled and tended each dusk.

locations.name: Harbour Board Hall
locations.description: The marble hall where curfews, tide tables and mooring licences are issued.

locations.name: Fog Wharf
locations.description: A timber wharf where fog off the estuary hides ships and smugglers alike, and where sailors swear the fog is haunted by the ghosts of the drowned.

locations.name: Tide-Clock Tower
locations.description: A brass clock tower whose gearing tracks the tides and sets the city's curfew bell.

factions.name: Lamplighters' Guild
factions.description: A guild that fills, lights and locks the city's gas lamps.

factions.name: Harbour Board
factions.description: Officials who issue curfews and mooring licences, and profit from both.

factions.name: Fog Runners
factions.description: Smugglers who use the curfew gaps to slip cargo past the wharf.

rules.statement: The city is lit by coal gas and driven by clockwork and steam.
After the curfew bell, wharf gates are locked until dawn and may be opened only by a Harbour Board officer's key.
Each lamp-house is locked at dusk with a guild key; only the lamplighter assigned to it and the guild master hold keys.
Fog thickens on the wharf at the turn of the tide, hiding ships for about an hour.

history.name: Laying of the Gas Mains
history.description: The Harbour Board laid the first coal-gas mains along Lamp-House Row.

history.name: Raising of the Tide-Clock
history.description: Clockmakers raised the Tide-Clock Tower and tied the curfew bell to its tide gearing.

history.name: The Lamplighters' Charter
history.description: The Lamplighters' Guild won a charter granting its members exclusive keys to the lamp-houses.

history.name: The First False Curfew
history.description: The Harbour Board secretly rang an early curfew bell so that the Fog Runners could bribe an officer to unlock the wharf gates.

conflicts.name: The False Curfews
conflicts.description: The Lamplighters' Guild accuses the Harbour Board of selling false curfews.

conflicts.name: The Wharf Smuggling
conflicts.description: The Harbour Board quietly tolerates the Fog Runners' smuggling in return for bribes.

evidence_quotes: sailors swear the fog is haunted by the ghosts of the drowned
traps.why_not_a_defect: An attributed superstition, not a world fact.

evidence_summary: The haunting is explicitly what sailors swear, an in-world belief; nothing supernatural is asserted as fact.
